comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 major requirements for 2025-2026 entrants; unresolved cohort credit allocation
comparator.sourceNotes: The current catalogue (12 May 2026), pp. 6-7 and 28-29, assigns its 75-EC Sustainability major to students who entered in 2025-2026. Their first-year requirements come from the 2025-2026 catalogue, whose p. 6 states a 45-EC core and 60 EC of choice, while pp. 9 and 57-61 identify only eight 5-EC core courses and a zero-credit Personal Development Track. CAP400 in the current catalogue (p. 120) still requires 110 EC including 45 EC of Academic Core. The new 2026 entrants have a 40-EC core and 65 EC of choice, but their major requirements will be set by the 2027-2028 catalogue. Combining that core with the older cohort’s major does not verify one complete pathway. The current catalogue webpage links no corrected edition. MyEUR redirects to institutional sign-in; the public ESSB EER explicitly excludes EUC. This record preserves only the 175 EC supported for the 2025 entrant framework: 40 identified core EC, the current 75-EC major and the stated 60-EC choice allocation. The missing 5 EC are not invented. Sustainability requires Basics of Life; 300-level courses require 60 prior EC. Major choice is 20 EC with at least 10 EC at 300 level; the four selected courses meet that condition. Politics of Public Policy requires SBS208, to be accommodated earlier within choice space. ECB313 cannot overlap MINUC-03. Exchange/off-campus study is limited to 30 EC overall and 15 EC within the major, with approval. The remaining formal credit/cohort questions prevent certification.

routeSelection.basis: The generic LAS target requires one current major. Sustainability is the current major whose official description most explicitly represents the programme’s broad academic identity by integrating Life Sciences, Social Sciences, Economics and Humanities in one multi-perspective framework. The route was selected independently of UCR fit. This remains a representative published major, not a certified whole-cohort180EC plan.

audience.programmeDescription: Erasmus University College offers a Liberal Arts and Sciences degree with an academic core, a declared major, research and elective study across humanities, social sciences, life sciences and economics. Its Sustainability major connects environmental, social, economic and historical inquiry.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is withheld while the published cohort requirements remain inconsistent. The UCR study possibilities have been preserved for reassessment; this is not a judgment that UCR offers no suitable programme.

curriculum.limitation: The identified components account for 175 EC. The 2025 entrant catalogue states a 45-EC core but lists only 40 EC, while the current major applies to that cohort. Official clarification of the remaining 5 EC and the applicable graduation rules is required. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified degree plan.

componentNotes.euc-first-electives: 15 EC of first-year elective study in the published 2025 entrant framework; the complete first-year allocation requires clarification.
componentNotes.euc-advanced-choice: 45 EC of later choice space in the stated 60-EC elective framework. Prerequisites and approval rules constrain choices.
componentNotes.euc-cap400: Individual 15-EC research thesis related to the major. Entry requires 110 EC including 45 EC of Academic Core; the core-credit discrepancy remains unresolved.
